title: Fifty Famous People
sourceTitle: Fifty Famous People: A Book of Short Stories
author: James Baldwin
licenseEvidence: Project Gutenberg #6168: 'Public domain in the USA'; first published by the American Book Company in 1912
description: James Baldwin's gentle companion to Fifty Famous Stories: true-to-life short tales about real people, from Lincoln rescuing baby robins to Ben Franklin's whistle and Caedmon singing in the cow shed. Each day you read a story or two aloud, your child tells it back, and then draws or copies something from it. A warm first taste of history for ages 6 to 9, and the full text is free online.
includes: 28 lessons in 6 units covering every story in the book
Link to the free full text for every story
A narration step and a drawing, copywork, or map step each lesson
Two or three questions per lesson, with answers
Parent notes on legends and dated passages

units.title: Unit 1: Kind Hearts and Clever Words

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Saving the Birds and Another Bird Story
steps: Read “Saving the Birds” and “Another Bird Story” aloud together
Tell back both stories: the lawyer in the muddy grove, then the general on the battlefield
Draw a nest put safely back in a tree
questions: What did Abraham Lincoln do for the baby robins?
Where did General Lee put the fallen nest?
answers: He climbed the tree and put them back in their nest
In the fork of a tree, where it would be safe
lessons.notes: Robert E. Lee was the leading general of the Confederate army in the Civil War. Baldwin, writing in 1912, praises him without that context; older children can talk about it.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Speaking a Piece and Writing a Composition
steps: Read “Speaking a Piece” and “Writing a Composition” aloud together
Narrate how each boy got ready for his schoolwork
Try the teacher's plan: pick one thing you can see, write its name, and say what it is like and what it is good for
questions: Who wrote the little speech for Edward Everett?
What did Henry Longfellow write his composition about?
answers: Mr. Harris, the minister
A turnip in Mr. Finney's garden

lessons.title: Lesson 3: The Whistle and The Ettrick Shepherd
steps: Read “The Whistle” and “The Ettrick Shepherd” aloud together
Tell back how Benjamin spent his pennies, then how Sirrah saved the lambs
Copy one line of “A Boy's Song” in your best handwriting
questions: What did Benjamin Franklin buy with all his pennies?
How many lambs did Sirrah keep safe in the ravine?
Why was James Hogg called the Ettrick Shepherd?
answers: A whistle
All seven hundred; not one was missing
He kept sheep near the Ettrick Water

lessons.title: Lesson 4: The Caliph and the Poet, “Becos! Becos! Becos!”, A Lesson in Humility
steps: Read “The Caliph and the Poet”, “Becos! Becos! Becos!”, and “A Lesson in Humility” aloud together
Narrate one of the three stories, whichever your child liked best
Find Egypt and Baghdad on a map or globe
questions: Why did the poet beg the caliph to keep his third wise saying?
What did the wise man say “becos” meant?
Why did Haroun-al-Raschid weep at his feast?
answers: Each saying was costing him a hundred gold pieces, and he wanted the gold
Bread
The poet reminded him that all his riches would be like a shadow when he died
lessons.notes: Baldwin himself points out that the king's experiment “proved nothing.” Ask your child why.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: The Midnight Ride
steps: Read “The Midnight Ride” aloud together
Have your child tell the story in order, from the secret visit to the ride through the night
Draw the church tower with its lanterns
questions: What did two lanterns in the church tower mean?
What were the king's soldiers going to Concord to take?
What did Paul Revere shout as he rode?
answers: The soldiers would cross the river
The gunpowder stored there
That the soldiers were coming and people should get up and defend themselves

lessons.title: Lesson 6: The Boy and the Wolf and Another Wolf Story
steps: Read “The Boy and the Wolf” and “Another Wolf Story” aloud together
Tell back both wolf hunts. Which one had a real wolf?
Draw Israel Putnam crawling into the cave with the rope around his waist
questions: What was Gilbert's “wolf” really?
How did the farmers know it was always the same wolf?
Why did Putnam tie a rope around his waist?
answers: A pet calf
Her tracks showed three toes missing from one front foot
So his friends could pull him out of the cave quickly

lessons.title: Lesson 7: The Horseshoe Nails and The Landlord's Mistake
steps: Read “The Horseshoe Nails” and “The Landlord's Mistake” aloud together
Narrate how one missing nail lost a kingdom
Copy the first two lines of the “want of a nail” rhyme
questions: How many nails did the smith put in the last two shoes?
Why did the landlord turn Mr. Jefferson away?
Why wouldn't Jefferson come back to the first hotel?
answers: Three in each, six in all
He was muddy and plain, and the landlord thought he was a poor farmer
If there was no room there for a farmer, there was no room for him

lessons.title: Lesson 8: A Lesson in Manners and Going to Sea
steps: Read “A Lesson in Manners” and “Going to Sea” aloud together
Act out Dean Swift's lesson: one person knocks rudely, then politely
Tell back why George Washington stayed home
questions: How did Dean Swift teach the messenger manners?
Why did George Washington change his mind about going to sea?
answers: They traded places, and the Dean showed him how to deliver a gift politely
He saw his mother crying and could not bear her sadness
lessons.notes: “Tom,” the boy waiting at the door in the Washington story, was almost certainly enslaved; the Washingtons owned slaves. A good moment to say so plainly.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: The Shepherd-Boy Painter and Two Great Painters
steps: Read “The Shepherd-Boy Painter” and “Two Great Painters” aloud together
Narrate the painted fly, then the painted curtain
Try to draw something so real it could fool someone: a fly, a cherry, or a sheep
questions: What was Giotto drawing on the rock when Cimabue found him?
What trick did Giotto play on his master's painting?
How did Parrhasius fool Zeuxis?
answers: A sheep
He painted a fly on the man's nose
He painted a curtain so real that Zeuxis asked to have it pulled aside

lessons.title: Lesson 10: The King and the Bees and Our First Great Painter
steps: Read “The King and the Bees” and “Our First Great Painter” aloud together
Tell back how the bees answered the queen's riddle
Draw a picture of a sleeping baby or a family member, as Benjamin West did
questions: How did Solomon find out which wreath had real flowers?
What did Benjamin West use to draw his baby sister?
answers: He opened the window, and the bees flew to the real flowers
A piece of charcoal on a smooth board

units.title: Unit 3: Learning and Telling the Truth

lessons.title: Lesson 11: The Young Scout and The Lad Who Rode Sidesaddle
steps: Read “The Young Scout” and “The Lad Who Rode Sidesaddle” aloud together
Narrate how each boy faced something he did not want to do
Draw Daniel Webster on the old gray horse
questions: What did the British captain order Andrew Jackson to do?
Why did Daniel Webster have to ride a sidesaddle?
Where was Daniel going?
answers: Clean the mud off his boots
The horse was being taken to Exeter for a lady to ride back on
To the academy at Exeter

lessons.title: Lesson 12: The Whisperers
steps: Read “The Whisperers” aloud together
Have your child tell the story, slowing down for the last minute before the bell
Talk together: was Elihu's whisper right or wrong?
questions: What was the rule of the master's new game?
Why did Elihu Burritt whisper on purpose?
What was Elihu later called?
answers: Whoever was standing when school ended would be punished for everyone
To take Lucy's place so she would not be punished
The Learned Blacksmith
lessons.notes: The schoolmaster threatens a “thrashing.” You may want to talk about how schools have changed.

lessons.title: Lesson 13: How a Prince Learned to Read and “Read, and You Will Know”
steps: Read “How a Prince Learned to Read” and “Read, and You Will Know” aloud together
Tell back how Alfred won the book
Copy the mother's saying, “Read, and you will know”

links.label: Read “How a Prince Learned to Read”

questions: Who taught Alfred to read?
What did Alfred's mother promise the book to?
About how many languages could William Jones speak and write?
answers: Brother Felix, a monk
The son who first learned to read it
Forty

lessons.title: Lesson 14: The Young Cupbearer and The Sons of the Caliph
steps: Read “The Young Cupbearer” and “The Sons of the Caliph” aloud together
Narrate what Cyrus did with the feast and how he served as cupbearer
Draw the two princes each carrying one of their teacher's shoes
questions: What did Cyrus do with the food from the feast?
Why didn't Cyrus taste the wine first?
How did the two princes settle who would carry the teacher's shoes?
answers: He gave it away to people who had been good to him and his mother
He thought it was poison because it made people act foolishly
Each carried one shoe
lessons.notes: Cyrus calls wine “poison” because of how it made the guests act. Explain as much as suits your child.

lessons.title: Lesson 15: The Boy and the Robbers and A Lesson in Justice
steps: Read “The Boy and the Robbers” and “A Lesson in Justice” aloud together
Tell back how Otanes kept his gold by telling the truth
Talk together: whose idea of justice was better, the shah's or Alexander's?
questions: Where had Otanes hidden his gold?
Why did the robber chief give the gold back?
What did the shah decide about the buried treasure?
answers: Under the lining of his hat
He admired the boy for telling the truth when a lie would have been easy
The first man's son should marry the second man's daughter and have it as a wedding gift

lessons.title: Lesson 16: The General and the Fox and The Bomb
steps: Read “The General and the Fox” and “The Bomb” aloud together
Narrate how Aristomenes found his way out of the chasm
Draw the fox running through the narrow passage with the general behind
questions: How did Aristomenes find the way out?
What did King Charles want his officer to keep doing after the bomb fell?
answers: He held onto a fox's tail and followed it through a hidden passage
Keep writing the order

lessons.title: Lesson 17: A Story of Old Rome
steps: Read “A Story of Old Rome” aloud together
Have your child tell the story: who went out to beg Coriolanus, and who finally changed his mind
Find Rome on a map of Italy
questions: Why were the Roman people angry at Coriolanus?
Who finally made Coriolanus turn his army back?
answers: He said the starving poor should have to pay for the corn
His mother and his wife (with his children)

lessons.title: Lesson 18: Saved by a Dolphin and “Little Brothers of the Air”
steps: Read “Saved by a Dolphin” and “Little Brothers of the Air” aloud together
Narrate Arion's story, then tell both ways it might have ended
Draw Arion riding the dolphin, or St. Francis with the birds
questions: What favor did Arion ask before he jumped into the sea?
What did St. Francis call the birds?
answers: To sing one last song
His little brothers (and sisters) of the air
lessons.notes: Baldwin gives two explanations for Arion's rescue, a dolphin or a ship named the Dolphin, and lets the reader choose. Ask which your child believes.

lessons.title: Lesson 19: A Clever Slave, One of Aesop's Fables, The Dark Day
steps: Read “A Clever Slave”, “One of Aesop's Fables”, and “The Dark Day” aloud together
Narrate why Aesop chose the biggest bundle
Draw the lawmakers working by candlelight on the dark day
questions: Why was Aesop's big bundle the best one to carry?
In the fable, what did the Mice plan to hang on the Cat?
What did Abraham Davenport ask for when the sky went dark?
answers: It held the food, so it got lighter at every meal
A bell
That the candles be lighted so they could keep working
lessons.notes: Aesop was enslaved. Baldwin tells the story lightly; you can talk about what it meant to be a slave and to be sold.

lessons.title: Lesson 20: The Surly Guest and The Story of a Great Story
steps: Read “The Surly Guest” and “The Story of a Great Story” aloud together
Tell back how Alexander Selkirk ended up alone on an island
Draw Selkirk's island, with his hut, garden, and goats

links.label: Read “The Story of a Great Story”

questions: Why did the innkeeper not tell Mr. Randolph which road to take?
How long did Selkirk live alone on the island?
What famous book grew out of Selkirk's story?
answers: Randolph had been rude when the innkeeper asked which way he was going
Four years and four months
Robinson Crusoe, by Daniel Defoe

lessons.title: Lesson 21: The King and the Page and The Hunted King
steps: Read “The King and the Page” and “The Hunted King” aloud together
Narrate what King Frederick found by the sleeping page
Draw the woman's farmhouse where Robert the Bruce found shelter
questions: What did the king put in Carl's pocket?
Why did the woman welcome every traveler?
Whose voice did Bruce hear outside the door?
answers: Ten gold pieces wrapped in his mother's letter
For the sake of one: Robert the Bruce
His brother Edward's

lessons.title: Lesson 22: “Try, Try Again!” and Why He Carried the Turkey
steps: Read “Try, Try Again!” and “Why He Carried the Turkey” aloud together
Tell back how many times the ant tried before it made it
Copy “Try, try again” and draw the ant with its grain of wheat
questions: How many tries did the ant need?
Who was the old man who carried the turkey?
Baldwin asks what other story “Try, Try Again!” is like. Which one?
answers: Twenty-one
John Marshall, Chief Justice of the United States
Robert the Bruce and the spider

lessons.title: Lesson 23: The Paddle-Wheel Boat and The Caliph and the Gardener
steps: Read “The Paddle-Wheel Boat” and “The Caliph and the Gardener” aloud together
Narrate how the merchant's money bag flew away and came back
Draw the fishing boat with a paddle wheel on each side
questions: What did Robert Fulton invent when he grew up?
What carried off the merchant's bag of gold?
How many gold pieces had the gardener borrowed?
answers: The steamboat
An eagle
Ten

lessons.title: Lesson 24: The Cowherd Who Became a Poet
steps: Read both parts of “The Cowherd Who Became a Poet” aloud together
Have your child tell why Caedmon hid in the cow shed and what happened there
Draw Caedmon singing among the cows

links.label: Read “The Cowherd Who Became a Poet”

questions: Why did Caedmon slip away from the kitchen?
What did the voice in his dream tell him to sing about?
Who had Caedmon's song written down?
answers: He was afraid of being asked to sing
The creation of the world
The abbess, who had her clerk write it

lessons.title: Lesson 25: The Lover of Men
steps: Read “The Lover of Men” aloud together
Have your child tell the three things Gautama saw outside the palace
Talk together: why had his parents kept him inside the walls?
questions: What three kinds of people did Gautama see on his ride?
What did Gautama decide to do with his life?
answers: An old man, a sick man, and poor men working on the road
Give everything to help people and ease their sorrow
lessons.notes: Gautama is the Buddha. Baldwin tells the story without naming the religion that grew from his teaching; you can add as much as suits your family.

lessons.title: Lesson 26: The Charcoal Man and the King
steps: Read “The Charcoal Man and the King” aloud together
Have your child narrate it, saving the surprise for the end
Draw the little king leaving in Charlot's Sunday suit

links.label: Read “The Charcoal Man and the King”

questions: Where did Jacquot find the child?
Who was the child?
What did the little king promise the family?
answers: In the fountain pool in the park behind the palace
Louis the Fourteenth, the king of France
Money for a bigger house and school for the boys

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Which Was the King? and The Golden Tripod (Part I)
steps: Read “Which Was the King?” and “The Golden Tripod” aloud together (stop at Part II)
Narrate the joke the boy made about the hats
Draw the fishing net coming up with the golden tripod in it
questions: How did King Henry say the boy would know the king?
What was in the fishermen's net?
Who did the oracle say should get the tripod?
answers: The king would be the only one with his hat on
A golden tripod and no fish
The wisest of the wise

lessons.title: Lesson 28: The Golden Tripod (Parts II–VII)
steps: Read Parts II to VII of “The Golden Tripod” aloud together
Have your child name, in order, each wise man the tripod was taken to
Look over the list “Fifty Famous People” at the end of the book and pick a favorite person
questions: Did any of the wise men keep the tripod?
Where did the tripod end up?
What are these seven men called?
answers: No, every one of them sent it on to someone else
In the Temple of Apollo at Delphi
The Seven Wise Men of Greece
